recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Shared types & data-access foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: Create src/shared/types/ (enums, DTOs, ValidationResult) and src/shared/db/ IUnitOfWork + base repository. No dependencies on domain modules; everything else depends on these.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Audit module
recommended_phases.rationale: AuditLog entity + repository + AuditService implementing AuditServiceInterface. Depends only on shared-types/shared-db; required by every state-changing service.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Employee entity + repository + service. Depends on shared-types/shared-db; provides manager lookup and active-status checks used by leave.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: LeavePolicy entity + repository + service. Depends on shared-types/shared-db; supplies entitlement and approval rules to leave.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: LeaveBalance entity + repository + service. Depends on shared-types/shared-db; provides commit/release/sufficiency used transactionally by leave.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6 — Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Notification entity + repository + service. Depends on shared-types/shared-db; fanout on approval/rejection.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7 — Auth & RBAC
recommended_phases.rationale: Auth middleware + requireRole guard. Depends on shared-types; consumed by leave routes.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 8 — Leave module (domain + service)
recommended_phases.rationale: LeaveRequest entity + repository + LeaveService. Depends on all prior modules; orchestrates transactions, audit, balance, policy, employee, notification.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 9 — Leave controller & routes
recommended_phases.rationale: LeaveController + routes wiring LeaveService with auth/RBAC and API-boundary validation. Depends on leave service and auth.

app_notes: Application slice for the leave management module. Layer boundaries: presentation (controllers/routes), application (services), domain (entities), infrastructure (repositories, IUnitOfWork, db). Dependencies flow inward only; leave (outermost) depends on audit/balance/policy/employee/notification/auth and shared-types/shared-db, none of which depend back on leave — no cycles. Shared pure value types (enums, DTOs, ValidationResult) live in src/shared/types/; entities with owned behavior live in their own module. Cross-module access is via public service interfaces only (e.g. leave calls BalanceService.commitDays, never BalanceRepository). Transactions are service-owned via injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction, with participating methods taking an optional client. Every state change writes an audit record via AuditServiceInterface.record. Canonical entity names adopted: LeaveBalance, LeavePolicy, AuditLog (reconciling DOMAIN.md duplicates).

open_questions.question: Which validation library should be standardized for API-boundary input validation?
open_questions.impact: Determines the validation approach in leave controller/routes; package.json lists both zod and class-validator (plus express alongside Fastify).

open_questions.question: What are the canonical names for duplicate/overlapping domain entities (Balance vs LeaveBalance, Policy vs LeavePolicy, Audit vs AuditLog vs AuditRecord)?
open_questions.impact: Affects entity/repository naming and table names; DOMAIN.md defines overlapping shapes that must be reconciled to one canonical entity each.

open_questions.question: Should package.json name be changed from leave-management to trackeros, and should express/class-validator/zod be pruned to match the declared Fastify stack?
open_questions.impact: Affects dependency hygiene and package identity; mismatched deps may cause lint/typecheck noise.
candidate_options: Rename to trackeros and prune express/class-validator/zod

open_questions.question: What is the exact error response shape beyond the required 400/401/403/404 status codes?
open_questions.impact: Determines the shared error type contract consumed by controllers and the @trackeros/contracts surface.

open_questions.question: Should the existing uptime module be refactored to the canonical repository/controller pattern, or left as-is?
open_questions.impact: Affects scope; new modules follow canonical pattern regardless, but uptime currently lacks repository/controller layers.

open_questions.question: Is the shared @trackeros/contracts package already scaffolded, or does it need to be created?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the typed REST surface must be built as part of this feature.

open_questions.question: What background jobs, if any, are required via BullMQ for leave/expense workflows (accrual schedulers, notification fanout)?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether a jobs module and BullMQ wiring are in scope for this feature.
candidate_options: No background jobs in this feature

open_questions.question: How should local development auth be implemented concretely (seeded local users vs mock OIDC provider)?
open_questions.impact: Affects the auth module implementation and dev setup for the JWT/OIDC strategy.

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole } where UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. Identity obtained from a JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware that populates request.user; RBAC enforced by a route-level requireRole(...) guard (never inline in handlers/services).
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure -> HTTP 400; authentication failure -> 401; authorization failure -> 403; not found -> 404.
